notes.summary: Fixes the actual bounded geometric domain from qualified G331, retaining all supports and conductor fibres, with n−1 potential entries and an explicit degree-n component convention. No product theorem is imported.
notes.detailedSummary: Uses only G331's independently defined Cartier-positive core, its uniform comparison, actual decreasing-net completion, compact boundary, density, gauge changes and full descent. Bounded inputs must belong to that actual geometric completion; zero and mixed-zero inputs are admitted, while all inputs with unbounded or bottom values are excluded. Dimension zero is empty and dimension one has zero potential entries.
notes.text:
Let (R,m) be an excellent reduced local ring of dimension n>0 and fix a proper m-primary ideal a. Write X_a={v:v(a)=1}, retaining every centred real semivaluation support, including nonminimal supports and supports on the conductor quotient. Primary ideal values are finite positive continuous functions on this compact Hausdorff space.

The sole incoming correctness/source grant is qualified G331, including its entire source, mandatory annotation, source ledger and exact scope. It defines positivity before ideal closure, using actual negative effective finite REAL Cartier presentations on actual primary blowups and nonnegative degree on every contracted proper integral curve. It proves C_geom=C_ideal and D_geom=D_ideal. Here C is the uniform closure of finite nonnegative real combinations of negative primary-or-unit ideal values, and D consists of infima of ACTUAL nonempty decreasing C-nets. No envelope, product, intersection, locality, energy or arbitrary-model cofinality result is imported.

The input domain is D_a^bd={u in D:-M≤u≤0 for some finite M}. Membership in D remains mandatory. Thus the construction below covers arbitrary real continuous C inputs and bounded completed inputs, including permitted zero and mixed-zero patterns; it does not declare every bounded nonpositive function geometric. Inputs with any −∞ value, including bottom, and unbounded inputs are excluded. If g_alpha decreases to u≥−M, each representing term already lies in [−M,0], so no unproved truncation or completion operation is needed.

Set p=n−1. A measure has p potential entries; its test supplies the nth intersection entry. All multiplicities below use the degree-n part of the primary length polynomial. In a non-equidimensional ring, lower-dimensional components remain in the boundary and function class but contribute zero in this convention. Separate products on those components would require their separate dimension-dependent arities. Dimension one has zero potentials and a reference measure. Dimension zero has empty centred boundary and the unique zero measure, without negative arity.

Two functional results of G331 are used. Rational profiles −v(I)/k, with the unit ideal allowed, are uniformly dense in C. The rational difference span of ideal gauges is uniformly dense in all real continuous functions on X_a. After synchronizing denominators, a span element is (v(J)−v(K))/k. The identity min(v(I)−v(J),v(K)−v(H))=v(IH+KJ)−v(JH) gives the lattice property. Rational constants come from v(a)=1. The truncations v((f)+a^N)=min(v(f),N) separate all semivaluations, including infinite coordinates. G331's compact lattice argument therefore supplies density on the entire boundary, not a finite grid.

For finite normalization, G331 retains all local normal centres and FULL restriction fibres. Fibres are singletons at finite conductor value; at infinite conductor value they are precisely the conductor-quotient identification fibres. Both completed geometric classes descend exactly when constant on these whole fibres. The normalization identities below are applied to actual downstairs inputs and their pullbacks, without selecting lifts or deleting an infinity stratum.

Nilpotents are reduced away. No unreduced generic-length information is recovered from these boundary data. General finite-map geometric operators and energy remain separate P12.6 and P12.5 targets.

notes.summary: Proves a positive, well-defined primary mixed-multiplicity kernel at arbitrary characteristic and residue field. This is an algebraic result, without geometric intersection or locality conclusions.
notes.detailedSummary: Establishes symmetry, product/power linearity, single-slot monotonicity by simultaneous superficial choices, integral-closure invariance by a finite graded algebra argument, and all-support valuative well-definedness. Finite residue-field transfer is algebraic only. Unit slots have zero moments and lower-dimensional components contribute zero under the declared degree-n convention.
notes.text:
Use n1. Write e_R(I_1,...,I_n) for the coefficient with one entry of each primary ideal in the degree-n part of the multigraded length polynomial.

The exact current July 2024 Swanson–Huneke author source is retained locally. Complete Theorem 17.4.2 and Definition 17.4.3 give the polynomial for finite modules over arbitrary Noetherian local rings, with degree equal to the module dimension and degree-dim R mixed coefficients zero for smaller-dimensional modules. Complete 17.2.2 gives superficial choices in nonempty Zariski opens, with prescribed finite prime avoidance. Complete 17.2.4 and 17.4.6 give reduction of a mixed coefficient by a superficial element avoiding minimal primes, without Cohen–Macaulay or reduced quotient assumptions. Complete 8.4.2 permits the algebraic extension R(Z)=R[Z] localized at mR[Z]: dimension, primary ideals and finite lengths are preserved. A finite-length composition series tensors to one whose factors are kappa(m)(Z), proving length preservation directly. This extension is used only for algebraic proofs; no boundary identification across it is assumed.

Symmetry follows by relabelling polynomial variables. Substituting equal variables for I and J represents (IJ)^t. The coefficient with exponent one in this shared variable receives exactly the terms having exponent one in I or in J. Consequently e(IJ,I_2,...,I_n)=e(I,I_2,...,I_n)+e(J,I_2,...,I_n), and substitution t↦rt gives e(I^r,I_2,...,I_n)=r e(I,I_2,...,I_n). A unit slot contributes zero because the length polynomial is independent of its variable.

Here is single-slot monotonicity without a false coefficientwise inference from polynomial inequalities. Suppose J⊂K and fix the other n−1 ideals. Over an infinite residue field choose an element in I_2 superficial for BOTH tuples (I_2,I_3,...,I_n,J) and (I_2,I_3,...,I_n,K), avoiding all minimal primes. The complete 17.2.2 proof makes the allowed choices complements of finitely many proper vector subspaces of I_2/mI_2. Their intersection has a point over an infinite field. Quotient dimension drops by one: avoiding minimal primes gives the upper bound; lifting a parameter system from the quotient and applying the height theorem gives the lower bound. Both included ideals remain primary in the quotient. Apply 17.4.6 to both tuples and repeat in the remaining fixed slots. At dimension one, J^N⊂K^N gives length(R/J^N)≥length(R/K^N); dividing by N gives e(J)≥e(K). Hence e(J,I_2,...,I_n)≥e(K,I_2,...,I_n) in every dimension. Reducing a tuple of primary slots to a one-dimensional primary multiplicity also proves positivity. The complete one-variable Hilbert–Samuel statement/proof and positive leading coefficient, 11.1.3–5, were read. The nonreduced intermediate quotients are allowed by these sources.

Integral-closure invariance is separate. If K⊂overline(J), let L=J+K. Homogeneous ideal-integrality equations make R[Lt] finite graded over R[Jt]. Choose homogeneous module generators of degrees at most h. Their degree t+h coefficients give L^(t+h)⊂J^t for all t≥1. Also J^t⊂L^t. Multiplying by A=I_2^(t_2)...I_s^(t_s) gives
length(R/L^t A)≤length(R/J^t A)≤length(R/L^(t+h) A).
Along any ray of positive integral exponents, divide by the common parameter to power n. The fixed shift h does not change the top homogeneous part, so the top parts for J and L agree on every positive rational ray and hence as polynomials. Thus all relevant mixed coefficients agree. If J and K have equal integral closure, apply this argument to J+K from both sides. This requires neither normalized Rees-algebra finiteness nor coefficientwise monotonicity of arbitrary polynomial differences.

For primary-or-unit ideals, the exact all-support criterion is
v(K)≥v(J) on X_a iff K⊂overline(J).
For proper primary J, apply complete Swanson–Huneke 6.8.4 to each local domain R/P, P minimal. Each has positive dimension, and the image of a is nonzero primary. Normalizing its centred rank-one DVRs by a makes them actual boundary points. Complete 6.8.3 or 1.1.5 assembles componentwise integral dependence. Conversely, a monic ideal-integrality equation and the unique-smallest-term argument prove the value inequality after quotienting by ANY semivaluation support. Primary values are finite. Unit cases are immediate or impossible as appropriate. Using minimal-support DVRs to prove the criterion does not remove other supports from the domain.

For rational inputs u_i=−v(I_i)/k_i define
B_u(v(J))=e_R(I_1,...,I_p,J)/(k_1...k_p).
For p=0 this is e_R(J); a zero input represented by the unit gives zero for p≥1. Equal profiles, after integer powers, give equal ideal values, hence equal integral closures. Invariance and power linearity prove presentation independence. Every rational relation among ideal tests becomes v(A)=v(B) after synchronizing denominators and multiplying ideals, so the test functional is well-defined. If v(A)−v(B)≥0, then A⊂overline(B), A+B has the same integral closure as B, and inclusion monotonicity gives e(I_1,...,I_p,A)≥e(I_1,...,I_p,B). Therefore the functional is positive on the entire rational test lattice.

Input order follows as well: u≤w makes ideal-gauge moments for u at least those for w. For u=−v(I)/k and w=−v(J)/l, use I^l⊂overline(J^k) and divide the resulting inequality by kl. Addition of negative rational profiles corresponds to product ideals and is additive in each slot.

These arguments discharge the algebraic kernel independently of ROOT338. They do not prove independent Cartier intersection comparison or locality. Exact bodies, hashes, URLs and complete immediate application units are in inputs/primary and source-application-ledger.md. Rerun: python audit_inputs.py; python build_delivery.py. Execution is not mathematical verification.

notes.summary: Constructs finite positive moment measures for real C and actual bounded D inputs, with representation independence and weak descending-net continuity. They are not yet claimed to be geometric products.
notes.detailedSummary: Proves mass and negative-shift error bounds, uniform extension, actual decreasing-representation independence, bounded-domain additivity, and a majorant formula. The descending-net theorem requires a common finite bound and a specified limit belonging to bounded D. No increasing closure, arbitrary infimum closure, flattening, measure-order monotonicity, total-variation convergence, Cartier comparison or locality is asserted.
notes.text:
Use n1–n2. The positive rational test functional has mass B_u(1)=B_u(v(a)). For rational q>||f||_infinity, positivity of q±f gives |B_u(f)|≤q B_u(1), hence |B_u(f)|≤||f||_infinity B_u(1). Density from n1 extends it uniquely to a bounded real-linear functional on all continuous tests. Real linearity follows by rational scalar approximation. Positivity persists by approximating a nonnegative continuous function and adding a vanishing positive rational constant. The compact-Hausdorff Riesz correspondence identifies this functional with a finite positive Radon measure. This is ordinary functional background at its exact hypotheses; it supplies no geometric intersection theorem.

For rational tuples in [−M,0], input order against the constant −M gives
0≤B_u(v(J))≤M^p e_R(a repeated p times,J),
and mass≤M^p e_R(a).
For p=0 the factor is one. This is order of ideal-gauge moments, not order of measures.

If two rational tuples u,w in [−M,0] differ coordinatewise by at most epsilon, compare u_i−epsilon≤w_i and the reverse inequalities. Addition of the legitimate negative constant −epsilon=−epsilon v(a) and multilinear expansion give
|B_u(v(J))−B_w(v(J))|≤[(M+epsilon)^p−M^p] e_R(a repeated p times,J). (1)
Each nonempty subset S of shifted slots contributes at most epsilon^|S| M^(p−|S|) times that reference mixed multiplicity. Summing gives the displayed binomial expression. Use rational errors slightly larger than the actual error when necessary.

For arbitrary REAL C inputs, approximate uniformly by rational profiles. The approximants have a common bound [−M−1,0]. Estimate (1) makes every gauge moment Cauchy and independent of approximation. Difference-test values converge, positivity and the mass bound persist, and the resulting functional extends to a measure. Density and bounded masses give weak convergence on every continuous test. Passing to the limit with slightly enlarged bounds yields (1) for real C tuples. Symmetry, nonnegative real homogeneity, addition within the negative cone, and order on ideal moments pass to the limit. For addition approximate both summands and their sum; for real homogeneity approximate the scalar rationally. No singular transfer of BFJ multiplier approximation is used.

Now choose ACTUAL decreasing C-nets g_(i,alpha_i)→u_i for bounded u_i in D. Every representing term lies in [−M,0]. Use the finite product of their directed sets. For each ideal test v(J), its moments increase under refinement and are bounded by the preceding mass/moment estimate. Define B_u(v(J)) as their finite supremum. This is an increasing limit of bounded SCALARS, not an increasing function-class limit. Difference-test values converge by subtraction. Positivity and a common mass bound again give a finite positive measure, denoted nu_a(u_1,...,u_p).

Representation independence has an explicit compactness proof. Let g and f be two actual representations of the same bounded tuple. Fix indices beta_i and epsilon>0. The directed open sets {g_(i,alpha)<f_(i,beta_i)+epsilon} cover X_a because their limits satisfy u_i≤f_(i,beta_i). A finite subcover and directedness select one alpha_i for which the inequality holds everywhere. Thus g_(i,alpha_i)−epsilon≤f_(i,beta_i). Input order and the C shift expansion give
B_f_beta(v(J))≤sup_alpha B_g_alpha(v(J))+[(M+epsilon)^p−M^p] e_R(a repeated p times,J).
Take the supremum over beta, send epsilon to zero, and reverse the roles. All gauge moments agree, and density identifies the measures. The same proof with limits u_i≤w_i proves order on ideal-gauge moments throughout bounded D.

Addition of two actual decreasing C-nets, indexed by their finite product, is an actual decreasing C-net to their bounded sum. Hence that sum belongs to D by definition. Passing to scalar limits in C additivity proves bounded-D additivity. Scaling is handled similarly; scalar zero produces zero. Symmetry is immediate. The negative-constant expansion and (1) therefore remain valid on bounded D. No arbitrary nested-net flattening or infimum closure is used.

For each primary ideal J there is the exact formula
B_u(v(J))=sup{B_g(v(J)):g_i in C and g_i≥u_i for every i}. (2)
Every such majorant lies in [−M,0]. Order gives one inequality, while terms of a representing net give the other. This is a scalar formula and does not redefine D by all majorants.

The precise descending-net theorem is as follows. Suppose u_(i,lambda) in bounded D decreases pointwise to a SPECIFIED u_i in bounded D, and every term and limit has a common finite bound [−M,0]. Then nu_a(u_(1,lambda),...,u_(p,lambda)) converges weakly to nu_a(u_1,...,u_p). Membership of the limit is a hypothesis, not an inferred closure theorem.

To prove it, order bounds every gauge moment above by the target moment. Fix continuous C-majorants g_i≥u_i and epsilon>0. D functions are upper semicontinuous, so {u_(i,lambda)<g_i+epsilon} is open. These sets give directed covers. Compactness and the finite number of slots select one common lambda with u_(i,lambda)−epsilon≤g_i everywhere. Order and the bounded-D shift expansion imply
B_u_lambda(v(J))≥B_g(v(J))−[(M+epsilon)^p−M^p] e_R(a repeated p times,J).
Send epsilon to zero and take the supremum in (2). Gauge moments converge; density of their difference lattice and uniformly bounded masses give convergence on every continuous test. This is weak net convergence, not total-variation convergence.

Any globally zero entry annihilates the mixed measure for p≥1. Mixed-zero branch patterns belonging to G331's actual class are admitted. No unbounded or bottom input is added.

The conclusion is a bounded MOMENT-measure construction with proved continuity and algebraic presentation independence. Independent Cartier intersection comparison and actual open-set locality remain unproved. Artifacts: n3.md, argument.md, P12.4-paper.tex and native-notes.json. Rerun: python build_delivery.py.

notes.summary: Proves the exact one-factor primary-gauge change and residue-degree normalization identity for moment measures, plus bounded BFJ comparison at its published smooth characteristic-zero closed-germ hypotheses.
notes.detailedSummary: The gauge rule is nu_b=T_*[v_a(b)nu_a]. Normalization sums actual top-dimensional normal centres with residue-degree weights and retains full conductor fibres. No vertical generic degree or general finite-map theorem is introduced. Equality with BFJ is proved for all bounded completed inputs and all semivaluations only in the published smooth affine closed-germ algebraically closed characteristic-zero range; singular locality is not inferred.
notes.text:
Use G331 and n1–n3. Let a,b be proper PRIMARY gauges, d(v)=v(b) on X_a and T(v)=v/d(v). The function d is continuous and bounded above and away from zero. Transport homogeneous inputs by u_(i,b)(T(v))=u_(i,a)(v)/d(v). G331 preserves C and actual D representations under this change, and finite bounds remain finite.

The exact moment-measure change is
nu_b(u_b)=T_*[d nu_a(u_a)]. (3)
For a rational ideal tuple, pairing the right side against v_b(J) gives the integral of d(v)v(J)/d(v), hence exactly the same mixed multiplicity as the left side. Density proves equality of measures. Uniform and actual descending continuity from n3 extend it to every bounded D tuple: multiplication of tests by the fixed continuous bounded d commutes with weak limits. There is ONE factor d. For b=a^r, potentials on the new section divide by r and the transported measure multiplies by r. Substitution proves the gauge cocycle. No nonprimary denominator is used.

Let S be the finite normalization and q range over its local normal centres above m. Set f_q=[kappa(q):kappa(m)] and let rho_q be restriction from X_(aS_q). For the degree-n convention,
nu_(a,R)(u)=sum_(dim S_q=n) f_q rho_(q,*) nu_(aS_q,S_q)(rho_q^*u). (4)
All smaller-dimensional centres and their supports remain present; they have zero degree-n contribution, rather than an invented generic degree.

Here is the algebraic proof. Complete Swanson–Huneke 17.4.4 and 17.4.8 give exact-sequence additivity and top-dimensional minimal-prime associativity for mixed multiplicities of finite modules. At every minimal prime P of reduced R, R_P is its component field and S localized over P is that same field. Thus the generic module lengths for R and S are both one, giving e_R(I_1,...,I_n;R)=e_R(I_1,...,I_n;S). Equivalently, S/R is annihilated by a regular conductor element and has dimension less than n. For A=I_1^(t_1)...I_s^(t_s), the finite Artinian quotient S/AS decomposes into its local factors, and composition series give
length_R(S/AS)=sum_q f_q length_(S_q)(S_q/AS_q).
Comparing degree-n homogeneous coefficients gives e_R(I_1,...,I_n)=sum_(dim S_q=n) f_q e_(S_q)(I_1S_q,...,I_nS_q). Formula (4) follows for rational inputs by moments and density, and then for C and bounded D by their proved continuities. Pullback of a chosen downstairs decreasing representation remains an actual bounded decreasing representation on each centre.

This checks actual residue degrees, including inseparable degrees. It uses generic identity on reduced normalization component fields, not a general finite-map trace. Every conductor-infinite support remains; identified masses are added by pushforward. Inputs are actual pullbacks and therefore agree on their FULL fibres. No arbitrary upstairs operator-descent theorem or general P12.6 formula is claimed.

There is a further comparison in the EXACT published BFJ range: a smooth affine CLOSED germ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, dimension n≥2, initially with gauge m. G331 grants the full all-semivaluation class identification. BFJ's setting and complete Section 4, including immediate proofs of 4.1–4.9, were read. The source supplies independent Cartier intersections, their ideal comparison, a positive measure characterized by intersection moments, and continuity along decreasing nef families. Its 4.4 additivity proof explicitly uses smooth multiplier approximation, as Remark 4.5 records; this is not transferred to singular or positive-characteristic rings.

The mixed-multiplicity conventions agree in this regular range. Choose a superficial parameter sequence in the given ideals, as in complete Swanson–Huneke 17.4.7. Regularity gives Cohen–Macaulayness, so successive parameter elements are nonzerodivisors. Repeated 17.4.6 reduces the polynomial coefficient to its dimension-one formula with zero annihilator term, namely the length of the generic parameter quotient used by BFJ.

BFJ 4.7 therefore gives n2's moments for every rational ideal tuple, so density identifies its measure with nu_m. For C inputs, BFJ intersection order and additivity give the same negative-shift estimate (1), proving uniform weak continuity and equality. For any actual bounded decreasing C representations, associated Weil coefficients decrease at every divisorial valuation to those of the bounded limit. BFJ 4.4 applies to the finite product net with a fixed Cartier ideal test. Its proof gives decreasing FAMILIES: upper semicontinuity and monotonicity in the coefficient topology yield continuity for coordinatewise decreasing nets, not only the sequence statement in 4.8. Consequently gauge moments converge to the BFJ moments, and n3 plus density identifies the measures on every bounded completed input and all semivaluations. Equation (3) transports this comparison to other primary gauges.

This recovers the published BFJ operator and its smooth intersection comparison at its stated hypotheses. No actual singular Cartier comparison or open-set locality follows from this argument. BFJ Section 4 supplies no locality statement used here.

notes.summary: Constructs the actual geometric curve zero-potential reference measure, with independent real Cartier comparison, model independence, residue/gauge weights, and locality and continuity at zero arity.
notes.detailedSummary: For every excellent reduced local curve, proves mu_a=sum_q f_q ord_q(a) delta_(ord_q/ord_q(a)). A finite normalization graph and local snake-sequence length argument identify this with independent Cartier zero-cycle degree on every actual primary model. Treats full branch fibres, mixed-zero bounded profiles, smooth DVR and empty cases. A normalization of generic degree one and residue degree d demonstrates why residue weights are necessary. This is not a positive-arity higher-dimensional theorem.
notes.text:
Let R be an excellent reduced local curve, with finite normalization having DVR centres S_q. Put f_q=[kappa(q):kappa(m)] and a_q=ord_q(a)>0. Every centred semivaluation of a DVR is a positive multiple of its order: a nonzero element is a uniformizer power times a unit, and units have value zero. Its support cannot be the maximal ideal, because the boundary ideal would then have infinite value. G331's normalization presentation therefore identifies the ENTIRE boundary with the finite discrete branch set v_q=ord_q/a_q. A regular conductor element has finite order on every branch, so all fibres here are singletons. Branches mean local normalization centres, not merely minimal components.

Define geometrically, before ideal-moment comparison,
mu_(a,R)=sum_q f_q a_q delta_(v_q). (5)
These are actual residue-degree weights, with no vertical generic degree.

We prove independent Cartier comparison on any actual primary model Y=Bl_I R. The ideal IS is invertible on the semilocal normal curve, so the blowup universal property gives h:Spec S→Y. This morphism is finite: its graph is closed in Spec S×_R Y because Y is separated, and projection to Y is finite as a base change of normalization. Its finite closed image contains every generic component point of the reduced primary blowup, hence is all of Y. Locally it is the finite normal birational extension with the same total quotient fields, so it is normalization. This proves domination of the stated primary curve models directly; no higher-dimensional arbitrary-model cofinality is assumed.

For an effective integral exceptional Cartier divisor A on Y, define its independent Cartier zero-cycle degree by
Degree_R[A]=sum_y length_(O_(Y,y))(O_(Y,y)/(g_y)) [kappa(y):kappa(m)],
using regular local equations g_y. Its support is finite: the finite normalization surjects onto Y and has finite closed fibre. These local rings are reduced one-dimensional rings, and the quotients have finite length. Residue fields are finite over the base residue field. This is the ordinary actual Cartier zero-cycle, not a degree defined by moments.

For the normalization comparison put T=O_(Y,y), let N be its finite semilocal normalization, and C=N/T. The module C has finite length because normalization is generically identical on a reduced curve. Multiplication by the regular local equation g in 0→T→N→C→0 yields
0→C[g]→T/gT→N/gN→C/gC→0.
The multiplication sequence for finite-length C gives length(C[g])=length(C/gC), so length_T(T/gT)=length_T(N/gN). Its DVR factors give
length_T(N/gN)=sum_(q→y) [kappa(q):kappa(y)] ord_q(g).
Multiply by [kappa(y):kappa(m)] and sum. Thus
Degree_R[A]=sum_q f_q ord_q(h^*A). (6)
No normality or Cohen–Macaulay assumption on Y was used.

G331's actual Cartier order-unit assertion writes any integral exceptional Cartier divisor F as a difference of effective exceptional Cartier divisors. Extend (6) by differences and finite real linear combinations. Local orders are homomorphisms on actual Cartier divisors, so relations cause no ambiguity. G331's evaluation at a branch is f_F(v_q)=ord_q(h^*F)/a_q. Hence
Integral f_F dmu_(a,R)=Degree_R(F). (7)
Both sides are unchanged under any common primary-model pullback because the pullback to normalization is unchanged. This proves actual model independence and independent real Cartier intersection comparison in dimension one.

For a primary ideal J, one-variable multiplicity additivity on the finite generically rank-one normalization, or n4's degree-one coefficient formula, gives
 e_R(J)=sum_q f_q ord_q(J)=Integral v(J) dmu_(a,R).
Indeed each DVR has primary Hilbert function with leading coefficient ord_q(J). Thus the independently geometric measure (5) agrees with n3's zero-potential moment measure; it was not defined by assigning moments and renaming them intersections.

The bounded geometric class on this finite branch set is every finite nonpositive vector. Each DVR cone is all nonpositive constants, obtained from parameter powers with real coefficients; the semilocal class is their finite product. Singleton normalization fibres and G331's positivity descent give every such vector downstairs. The actual decreasing completion is every extended nonpositive vector; bounded vectors are already continuous. All-zero and mixed-zero profiles are allowed as boundary functions, without a literal radial-extension identification.

There are zero potential entries. Therefore any two zero-tuples give the same measure on every open region, proving actual locality at this zero arity; every bounded descending-net statement for the zero-tuple is constant equality. This is not advertised as a positive-arity Bedford–Taylor theorem. Continuous tests have the usual finite-set continuity.

For another primary gauge b, put b_q=ord_q(b). The section map sends v_q to ord_q/b_q and multiplies its mass by b_q/a_q, exactly equation (3). Normalization is equation (4) with weights f_q. A smooth DVR over its own residue field has mass a_q at ord/a_q; maximal-ideal reference mass is one. Dimension zero has empty boundary and the zero measure without negative arity.

Here is an actual nontrivial residue-degree example. For any finite field extension k⊂l of degree d>1, possibly inseparable, let R=k+t l[[t]]⊂S=l[[t]]. With A=k[[t]] and a k-basis 1,alpha_2,...,alpha_d of l, R=A⊕sum_(i≥2) tA alpha_i. It is a finite A-algebra, hence Noetherian and excellent. It is local with maximal ideal tS and residue field k: elements with nonzero constant in k have inverses with constant in k. Its fraction field is l((t)), since t alpha/t=alpha. Thus S is finite normalization with GENERIC degree one but RESIDUE degree d. The conductor is tS; a conductor unit would force l=k.

For a=tS, formula (5) is d delta_(ord_t). For J=t^rS, J^N=t^(rN)S. A k-basis of R/J^N consists of 1 and alpha_j t^i for 1≤i<rN and 1≤j≤d. Hence length_R(R/J^N)=1+d(rN−1) and e_R(J)=dr. This is the correct moment and Cartier degree. Replacing the residue weight by generic degree one would incorrectly give r.

notes.summary: Proves a nilpotent-data obstruction and a non-equidimensional top-degree degeneracy, and gives an exact diagnostic showing that positivity and continuity alone do not imply locality.
notes.detailedSummary: Identical reduced boundary/gauge data can have unreduced multiplicity one or two, requiring extra nilpotent length data. A dimension-two surface/curve fibre product has a nonzero curve-only bounded geometric input with zero degree-two moment measure. A two-point positive additive continuous map fails locality, but is not the actual kernel and does not disprove P12.4. Finite exact diagnostics passed on their expressly bounded domains.
notes.text:
These examples distinguish genuine obstructions from missing proofs. They do not establish impossibility of reduced higher-dimensional P12.4.

For nilpotents, take R_1=k[[t]] and R_2=k[[t]][epsilon]/(epsilon^2). Both are excellent local rings and (t) is primary in both. Their reduced gauges and centred semivaluation boundaries are identical, because nilpotents have infinite value. Nevertheless length_(R_1)(R_1/(t^N))=N and length_(R_2)(R_2/(t^N))=2N. The bases are respectively t^i and t^i,epsilon t^i, 0≤i<N. Their multiplicities are one and two. Thus an assignment depending only on G331's reduced boundary and reduced gauge cannot recover both unreduced intersection multiplicities. Extra generic-length data are necessary for that different target. This is not an obstruction to the explicitly reduced construction.

For the non-equidimensional convention, let R=k[[x,y,z]]/(xy,xz), isomorphic to k[[y,z]] fibre-product over k with k[[x]]. Restriction to the two components gives pairs with equal constant terms; its kernel is (x) intersection (y,z)=(xy,xz). The ring is reduced, excellent and complete, of dimension two. Its normalization is S=k[[y,z]]×k[[x]], finite with quotient S/R one copy of k. Its conductor is the pair of maximal ideals, corresponding downstairs to m=(x,y,z). Every centred boundary point has finite conductor value. Thus the full boundary is the disjoint union of the full surface boundary and the curve point, with singleton fibres and clopen pieces.

Use gauge m and I_N=(y,z,x^N). This is primary. The rational profile u_N=−v(I_N)/N is identically −1/N on the surface boundary and −1 at the curve point. It converges uniformly to a C function u that is zero on the surface and −1 on the curve. This uses uniform closure, not an assumed increasing D closure. Equation (4) gives e_R(I_N,m)=1: the surface restriction is its maximal ideal in both slots, whose degree-two multiplicity is one, while the curve contributes no degree-two coefficient. The surface calculation follows from length(k[[y,z]]/(y,z)^t)=t(t+1)/2. Hence nu_m(u_N) has mass 1/N, and positivity makes its weak limit zero. N3 therefore gives nu_m(u)=0 although u is nonzero. The lower-dimensional point remains in the boundary and function class; it has zero top-degree contribution rather than an invented vertical degree. A curve product there would require the separate zero-potential convention.

For the locality diagnostic, take the compact discrete two-point space K={x,y}, its cone of all finite nonpositive functions, and F(u)=(−u(x)−u(y)) delta_x. This map is positive, additive, nonnegative-real homogeneous, uniformly continuous and continuous for bounded decreasing nets. But u=(−1,−1) and w=(−1,−2) agree on the open set U={x}, whereas F(u)|_U=2 delta_x and F(w)|_U=3 delta_x. Thus those formal properties alone do not imply locality. This map is not asserted to satisfy the primary mixed-multiplicity kernel or to disprove locality of n3's actual moment construction. A separate geometric proof remains necessary.

Its observed output was PASS on 48 residue-degree basis cases (d=2,3; r=1,2,3; N=1,...,8), eight nilpotent basis cases (N=1,...,8), and 27 two-branch gauge/test combinations using exact fractions. It checks the basis slopes and the identity that old branch mass a_q multiplied by b_q/a_q becomes b_q and gives unchanged homogeneous test moments. This is exhaustive only on those declared finite arithmetic inputs. It neither proves arbitrary-real coverage nor geometric locality or higher-dimensional Cartier comparison.

The ENTIRE original P12.4 is not solved. Candidate=false.

The draft establishes an algebraic mixed-multiplicity kernel at every excellent reduced local ring, a unique positive moment-measure extension to real C inputs and bounded inputs in G331's ACTUAL decreasing completion D, a weak descending-net theorem with specified bounded-D limit, exact primary-gauge and residue-degree normalization identities, and equality with the exact published BFJ operator in its smooth affine CLOSED-germ algebraically closed characteristic-zero range. All supports and full conductor fibres are retained. Zero and mixed-zero inputs are admitted when in the actual class; unbounded and bottom inputs are excluded. Non-equidimensional rings use the explicit degree-n convention with n−1 potentials.

An actual independent geometric theorem is proved for all excellent reduced curves: the zero-potential reference measure, real Cartier zero-cycle comparison on actual primary models, model independence, exact gauge/normalization weights, and locality/continuity at zero arity. Dimension zero has empty boundary and zero measure. The nilpotent obstruction concerns only reconstruction of unreduced lengths from reduced data.

Two higher-dimensional obligations remain unresolved. First, prove that the extended kernel agrees with an independently defined local Cartier intersection for every actual negative curve-nef REAL Cartier presentation on an actual primary blowup, retaining nonnormal, non-Cohen–Macaulay, finite-residue-field and non-equidimensional issues. G331's uniform FUNCTION approximation does not establish INTERSECTION continuity. Uniform approximation by section-ideal evaluations does not by itself identify their multiplicities with an independent Euler-characteristic intersection. No arbitrary-model cofinality is available.

Second, prove actual open-set locality: if every pair u_i,w_i agrees on an open U in the normalized boundary, prove equality of the restrictions of their mixed measures to U. Positivity, global length polynomials, uniqueness of moment representation and weak convergence do not prove this. Even a core model-atom locality argument would need a further valid passage to arbitrary bounded completed inputs; neither step is supplied here. The diagnostic in n6 demonstrates the inadequacy of the bare formal properties, without disproving locality of the actual kernel.

Accordingly n3's measures are called MOMENT measures and are not promoted to the requested actual geometric products. Algebraic presentation independence is not relabelled geometric model-independent intersection theory. Missing proofs are not an impossibility verdict for reduced P12.4. P12.5 energy and general P12.6 operators remain separate.
